title: Add incident_type metric labels with cardinality guardrails + sampling
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Reliability Program: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
description:
Goal
- Enable incident reporting and dashboards to break down impact by incident_type/owner without exploding metric series.
- Add incident_type (and limited incident_subtype where appropriate) to a small set of reliability metrics / recording rules used for incident analytics, with hard guardrails:
  - allowlist only (v1 taxonomy)
  - bounded label sets
  - sampling/aggregation on high-volume signals
  - explicit unknown/unclassified buckets

Background / context
We want to answer: "What types of incidents are driving our availability/latency pain, and are we meeting remediation SLAs?" The taxonomy work makes incident_type required in incident-bot, but we also need a metric strategy so we can do reliable reporting in Grafana and avoid retroactive manual joins.

Constraint: cardinality
Adding incident_type to request-level histograms/counters can easily multiply series by existing labels (route/model/region/status_code/tier/customer). Observability has flagged we must keep v1 low-cardinality and enforce an allowlist at ingestion/emit time.

Scope (what we are labeling)
1) Primary: "incident analytics" metrics and recording rules (low volume)
- New/updated metrics emitted by incident-bot / incident event pipeline (per incident, not per request):
  - ri_incident_events_total{incident_id, incident_type, severity, tier, owner_team} (incident_id stored in logs only; NOT in metrics; see guardrails)
  - ri_incident_sla_breach_total{incident_type, severity, tier}
  - ri_incident_time_to_mitigate_seconds{incident_type, severity, tier}
  - ri_incident_time_to_fix_seconds{incident_type, severity, tier}
- NOTE: incident_id must NOT be a metric label. Incident-level joins should be done via incident timeline views / logs.

2) Limited: "key error/latency" service metrics (high volume)
- We will only attach incident_type to derived/recorded series used in dashboards/alerts, not to raw request metrics with large existing label sets.
- For redwood API gateway / router / runtime services, we will attach incident_type to:
  - request_errors_total ONLY for aggregated views with reduced dimensionality (drop route/model/customer labels)
  - error-budget burn recording rules (already aggregated)
  - alert evaluation outputs (alert payload already includes incident_type; metrics reflect alert->type attribution)

Implementation details
A) Allowlist + normalization
- Source of truth: v1 taxonomy allowlist is maintained as a static file in-repo (generated manually for v1; automate later):
  - incident_type_allowlist.yaml containing allowed incident_type + (optional) allowed incident_subtype
- Emission rules:
  - If incident_type is missing -> set incident_type="unknown"
  - If incident_type not in allowlist -> set incident_type="unknown" and increment ri_incident_label_rejected_total{reason="not_allowlisted"}
  - incident_subtype is only emitted for a small subset of categories where it materially helps routing/analysis AND the subtype count is bounded (<= ~40 total across all types). Otherwise subtype="n/a".

B) Cardinality guardrails (hard limits)
- Explicitly drop high-cardinality labels when incident_type is present (service-level reduced dims):
  - disallow: customer_id, request_id, prompt_hash, model_revision, route_id
  - keep: service, tier (hosted/dedicated/private), region, severity (for incident-derived metrics)
- Enforce a maximum distinct incident_type values at runtime (defensive):
  - if more than allowlist size observed in a process lifetime, stop emitting incident_type label and emit ri_incident_label_guardrail_tripped_total.

C) Sampling / aggregation strategy
- For request_latency_seconds_bucket and other histograms:
  - Do not add incident_type to raw histograms.
  - Instead, create recording rules that compute "incident attribution" on a periodic basis from incident windows (start/end timestamps) and aggregate to incident_type-level series.
- For request_errors_total:
  - We tested adding incident_type directly and saw a series jump when combined with route/model labels.
  - Final approach: emit incident_type on an aggregated error counter (no route/model/customer), and keep raw error counter untouched.

D) Review + ownership
- Observability review required (Allison Grant) before rollout to production.
- SRE (Aisha Bello) signs off on dashboard queries using the new series.

Rollout plan
1) Land code changes guarded behind feature flag: metrics.incident_labels_enabled=false by default.
2) Enable in staging; run synthetic incident drill (create incident, set incident_type, verify series appear).
3) Canary enable in one hosted region for 24h; monitor:
  - total active series count
  - top-N metric cardinality deltas
  - ingest volume + remote_write latency
4) Expand to all hosted regions; then dedicated; then private control plane components.
5) Publish final guidance in ops docs and link from incident-bot.

Success metrics
- Dashboard can show: incident volume + impact + SLA breaches by incident_type and owner_team with <5% "unknown" after 2 weeks.
- No sustained >2% increase in total active series in the primary Prometheus clusters.
- No increase in query latency/timeouts for existing reliability dashboards.

Out of scope (v1)
- Freeform labels/tags on metrics.
- incident_id as a metric label.
- Per-customer incident breakdown in metrics (must come from incident system / support tooling).
acceptance_criteria: incident_type is available as a bounded label (allowlist enforced) on incident analytics series used by the taxonomy dashboards
High-volume request metrics do NOT gain unbounded new label dimensions; raw histograms/counters remain unchanged or aggregated-only
unknown/unclassified behavior is well-defined and tracked via rejection/guardrail counters
Observability review completed and documented in ticket comments (cardinality delta + rollout approval)
Canary rollout completed with no cardinality regressions; feature flag enabled for hosted by default
Grafana taxonomy dashboards can break down impact/volume by incident_type with expected data (validated against 2–3 real incidents)
comments: 2025-12-11 (Rafael Mendes): Creating this as the follow-on to taxonomy definitions. Requirement from SRE: incident_type must show up in dashboards for incident volume + error-budget burn attribution, but we cannot explode series with route/model/customer labels.

2025-12-13 (Allison Grant): Strong -1 on adding incident_type to all request histograms. Please keep incident_type on low-volume incident/event metrics, and use recording rules for attribution. Also: no incident_id labels in metrics; logs only.

2025-12-18 (Sergio Costa): Draft implementation plan: (1) allowlist file, (2) aggregated error counter with incident_type, (3) recording rules for incident windows. Will share a before/after series count from staging once merged behind flag.

2026-01-07 (Sergio Costa): Opened PR redwood#28519 with initial label wiring for request_errors_total. Early staging results show label explosion when combined with route/model. Proposing to revert direct labeling and instead add an aggregated metric family (drop route/model/customer).

2026-01-10 (Allison Grant): Approved revised approach. Please also add ri_incident_label_rejected_total and a guardrail trip counter so we have an early warning if a bad deploy starts emitting unexpected types.

2026-01-22 (Sergio Costa): Landed observability-pack dashboards/alerts PR #1459 using the new incident-derived series. Still seeing elevated series count in one cluster due to a leftover label set; prepping follow-up.

2026-01-24 (Sergio Costa): Follow-up PR observability-pack#1467 reduces cardinality by removing route_id/model from the incident-attributed recording rule output. Canary looks stable (series delta ~+0.7%).

2026-02-07 (Aisha Bello): Validated against incidents #incidents/1763875520 and #incidents/1762959044. Dashboard breakdown matches incident-bot classification; unknown bucket <3% for last 7d. Marking done.
risk_notes: Primary risk is silent cardinality growth from (a) incident_type combined with existing high-cardinality labels, or (b) taxonomy churn leading to new label values. Mitigations: strict allowlist + normalization to unknown, explicit label drop list for incident-attributed series, guardrail counters + canary rollout, and keeping incident_id out of metrics entirely.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: staging validation + synthetic incident drill, 24h hosted-region canary with series-count monitoring, then global hosted enablement, followed by dedicated clusters. Private deployments only get the incident-derived series; request-level metrics remain unchanged. Any cardinality regression triggers immediate flag rollback and postmortem note in Observability weekly.
